sections.title: Local remediation, tiling and the memory wall

keyTerms.definition: Splitting matrices into SRAM-sized blocks. The tile size is the largest block with all live tiles fitting.
Softmax with a running max and normalizer. New blocks rescale old terms to the new max.
Tiled attention that never materializes the full score matrix. Outer loop over Q blocks, inner loop over K/V blocks.
Merging elementwise chains into one kernel. It streams the tensor once instead of once per op.
A tile-level GPU language. Each program instance handles one tile, tl.arange builds indices, tl.load/store move tiles.
Recomputing forward values in backward instead of storing them. It trades cheap FLOPs for bottlenecked HBM.

recall.question: What is the SRAM budget equation, and what does it decide?
recall.answer: tiles*B_c*d_h*bytes + stats <= SRAM. It sets the largest tile size with all live tiles resident.

recall.question: Why does FlashAttention backward recompute instead of storing?
recall.answer: Backward needs S and P per tile. Recomputing them from stored m and l trades FLOPs, which are cheap, for HBM, which is the bottleneck.

recall.question: What numerical rules keep tiled kernels safe in low precision?
recall.answer: Statistics m and l in fp32, accumulators in fp32, inputs and outputs in the working dtype.
